chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) used to spread [recite] with this supplication: You place your hand upon the place of the pain and you say
O pain, settle by the tranquility of Allah, and cool down by the dignity of Allah, and be barred by the barrier of Allah, and calm down by the calmness of Allah
I seek refuge for you, O human being, by what Allah, Exalted and Glorious, would be sought by His Throne and His Angels on the Day of the tremor and the earthquakes
You say that seven times, and not less than three
ai.seo_question: What is the specific supplication for curing illness by placing the hand on the affected area?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Shia tradition of using physical touch combined with verbal invocation for healing, emphasizing the concept of 'Sakinah' (tranquility) as a divine attribute that calms both physical pain and spiritual anxiety. The reference to the 'Day of Trembling' (Yawm al-Rajfah) connects the supplication to eschatological events, specifically recalling the stability of the Throne during cosmic upheavals, thereby grounding the healing ritual in the broader narrative of Allah's sovereignty. This practice reflects the Imami understanding of the Prophet's and Imams' authority to invoke divine names for tangible relief, serving as both a medical remedy and a spiritual anchor.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Haroun Bin Muslim, from Mas’ada Bin Sadaqa,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> that the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> used to seek cure with this supplication: ‘You should place your hand upon the place of the pain, and you should be saying,

‘O you pain! Settle by the Tranquility of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and cool down by the Dignity of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and be barred by the Barrier of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, calm down by the Calmness of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>.

Seek Refuge, O human being, by what Refuge of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> with Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would be sought by His<sup>azwj</sup> Throne, and His<sup>azwj</sup> Angels on the Day of tremors and earthquakes’.
You should say that seven times, and not less than three’.
en.sarwar: 17. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas’adah ibn Sadaqa from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “The Holy Prophet would seek cure with this supplication.

He would place his hand over the painful area and say, ‘O pain, calm down by the serenity of Allah, silence by the dignity of Allah, be barred by the barrier of Allah, quiet down by the calm of Allah, I protect you O human being by that with which Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has protected His Throne, His angels on the day of the shaking and quake.’
You should say it seven times or no less than three times.”
